headline: Kept its regular schedule; discussed snow removal in bike lanes, Bluebikes expansion, and bike racks.
summary: The group discussed a possible meeting with the DPW Director about winter snow removal and bike lanes. It also covered Bluebikes expansion talks, bike racks at Remond School, and upcoming events. One motion passed by unanimous vote to set the regular schedule.
decisions: Approved making 6:15 pm the regular meeting time, with all members voting in favor.

plain_text:
1 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
 
Salem Bicycling & Shared Path Advisory Committee 
 
Wednesday, September 2, 2026 | 6:15 p.m. 
 
City Hall Annex 1st Floor Meeting Room & Via Remote Participation 
 
Members Present: John Wathne (Chair), Josiah Guthrie (Vice Chair), Kevin Jordan, 
Craig Bilodeau, Alexa Ogno, Josh Nagle 
Members Absent:   Emmylou Manwill, Matt Caruso, Annie Wolf 
Also Present:  Tom Devine, Senior Planner 
 
Call Meeting to Order 
 
Wathne calls the meeting to order. 
 
Public Comment 
 
Stacy Kilb, the City’s Sustainability Engagement Coordinator, speaks about the 
upcoming Volt & Vibe PEV event at the bike path at the Salem State University Central 
Campus on September 19. Ogno is interested in tabling for the Committee. 
 
A member of the public speaks later in the meeting. She lives on Jefferson Ave. and 
works near the Lynn border. She advocates for bike lanes on Jefferson Ave. She notes 
that the website incorrectly lists the meeting start time as 6:30pm. Devine will correct 
this. 
 
Guthrie motions, Bilodeau seconds, and all vote in favor to make 6:15 pm their regular 
meeting time. 
 
Discussion of Bike Master Plan and Role of the Committee 
 
Guthrie suggests dedicating the time for this item to preparation for a discussion with 
the DPW Director. 
 
Devine spoke briefly with Patti Kelleher (Salem's Preservation Planner) about Friends of 
Greenlawn Cemetery to explore the non-profit model. The nonprofit status gave the 
group fundraising ability and they were instrumental in getting the cemetery listed on the 
National Register of Historic Places and designated as an arboretum. The status also 
gave the group some independence to speak with its own voice separate from the City. 
Volunteers established the non-profit on their own and complete regular annual 
reporting, which is understood to require substantial time and effort.
2 
 
Nagle adds from his recent experience establishing a non-profit that there is indeed 
some work involved. The group wonders whether it would make sense to instead join a 
chapter of a bigger nonprofit, like MassBike, League of American Bicyclists, or People 
for Bikes. Alexa may contact one of these groups. 
 
The group suggests Devine follow up to learn whether there is any limit on members of 
Friends of Greenlawn serving on the City’s Cemetery Commission. 
 
Discussion of Proposed Committee Logo 
 
Guthrie asks to take this of the future agendas. 
 
Bikeshare Program Updates 
 
Devine reports that he has met with staff from Beverly and Lynn to discuss potential 
Bluebikes expansion throughout the North Shore and is scheduled to meet with 
Swampscott. He also intends to contact other neighboring municipalities. Ogno requests 
information on e-bike ridership. Devine states that the Bluebikes station at Salem 
State’s North Campus was relocated permanently from the Alumni Plaza at the Campus 
Center to Loring Ave. in front of Meier Hall. 
 
Ogno expresses concern about the bike racks installed at Remond School. They are 
squiggly racks, not the more preferred and usable inverted U type. Devine expresses 
regret at not being involved to make sure all are aware that the Bike Committee has 
done previous work to make clear what types of racks are recommended. 
 
Events 
 
Ogno is planning a taco ride, tentatively scheduled for Sunday, September 27 at noon. 
The group wishes to participate in the October 1st Haunted Happenings Parade. Devine 
will register the group. 
 
Potential DPW Attendance at Future Meeting 
 
The committee discussed inviting the DPW Director to a future meeting to develop a 
collaborative approach to winter snow removal, particularly in bike lanes. Members 
emphasized that the conversation should be constructive rather than adversarial, with a 
clear agenda focused on identifying priorities such as keeping bike lanes and multiuse 
paths clear, addressing issues on North Street, exploring curb-to-curb plowing and 
enforcement options, and understanding DPW's operational challenges. The committee 
also wants to learn about DPW's resource needs and explore how it can support 
infrastructure design, public education, and advocacy for additional resources. Wathne 
may wish to prepare a letter of invitation, and the meeting would begin with 
introductions, appreciation for DPW's efforts, and a discussion of realistic expectations 
and opportunities for collaboration.
3 
 
Transportation Commission Update 
 
Ogno was not present at the most recent meeting. Topics included truck safety with side 
guards and signage as well as designated rideshare dropoff areas in downtown. 
 
Staff Update 
 
Devine passed along to colleagues the request to have a option in See-Click-Fix where 
one can request a bike rack the way there is to request a tree planting. Transportation 
Staff will be looking at potential new bike rack locations after October and suggestions 
from the Committee are welcome. 
 
Devine announces that the City is evaluating a potential contraflow bike lane on 
Goodhue Street when it is restriped, as suggested by Councilor Holappa. 
 
Devine notes that Manwill has resigned from the Committee and he expects her to 
remain on the Transportation Commission. 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
There are no draft minutes to review. 
 
Adjourn 
 
Bilodeau motions, Nagle seconds, and all vote in favor to adjourn at 7:25pm. 
 
*** 
 
Approved by the Bicycling & Shared Path Advisory Committee on 10/7/2026.
